commit_scope: Move Pulse web and its history upstream into one native Form read; retain exact history while removing repeated reads, hydration and external trace transport.

roles: native application source repair and delivery

evidence_refs: Native form-cli retrieval returned an insufficient dictionary/source-name hit. Repair reasoning and prose are rented OpenAI frontier output; exact model identity and task token counters are not exposed. Native execution supplied observations, not this response's generation.

The existing page made three parallel HTTP reads into a serial Pulse listener, decoded the complete silence window and hydrated the React tree. A native public trace read /pulse in 8320 ms with 1525401 body bytes. The new page composes now/history/silence evidence from one checkpoint directly in BML; escaped HTML, accessible daily evidence links, p50/p95 sparklines, current details and complete repair notes remain available. The thirty-silence display cap and the Next.js Pulse family/origin configuration are retired.

The first native HTML fixture rendered 37993 bytes in 105 ms with escaped markup and no script/hydration payload. A browser visual read confirmed the layout and accessible daily evidence links. That fixture is not a claim about full production-archive latency.

A weighted-selection experiment was exact but slower: all twelve archive organs matched the existing native histogram ranks, while selection took roughly twice the sort/merge time. It was removed. Daily cards and exact aligned range summaries now retain the existing histogram algebra at its publication owner; they are derived indexes, not TTL response caches or retention limits.

Native index construction against the private consistent archive completed across 185 populated days in 61341 ms. The existing raw ledger remained 6339890 samples. Native range comparison used one UTC cutoff and checked all twelve organs' 180 daily counts, failures, daily/window p50/p95 and window uptime against direct daily history plus the partial boundary day. All matched. Indexed 180-day history calculated in 2788 ms, compared with the preceding deployed 10342 ms read (different nearby snapshots; not a controlled benchmark).

The actual archive-backed HTTP observations returned the default page in 1622 ms (55662 bytes) and a selected day in 1642 ms (55907 bytes), without hydration. The full 180-day page returned 200 with 1087418 bytes in 9550 ms before the final whole-raw-page inclusion optimization. That longest HTML response remains a measured cost, not an artificially shortened window. Whole raw pages now reuse their committed min/max timestamps; only a straddling page parses each row time.

The same file-backed native task door used in service passed the focused application fixture on a fresh store after indexed publication changed: nearest ranks [20,30], supported windows, durable three-failure/three-success repair, and seven-row idempotent lost-checkpoint/torn-tail replay. Startup compares raw-day sequence coordinates and the organ catalog to reconcile older-writer deltas before serving indexed reads.

The plain native client accepted a header packet as a complete response because the old helper treated an absent case-sensitive Content-Length match as completion. Exact observation: internal ideas requests returned status 200 with zero body bytes while public requests held 2276 bytes. Application-owned wr-receive now reads through the explicitly requested HTTP/1.0 close using balanced spans. The changed native HTML observations verify complete closing document bytes. The external curl trace was retired in favor of native parallel request workers with private complete body/header captures and honest total/serving timing.

Source repairs retained exact failures: form-run ./fkwu --check ../pulse/read.bml reported unbound high-low, v-low and i-1; spacing restored their intended arithmetic. The first trace source reported a mismatched delimiter and was repaired at that expression. A private rehearsal's obsolete config.local.json caused /state.fkb to be missing after a directory copy; that superseded private config was retained outside active source rather than changing production defaults. The actual immutable build copies only committed production configuration.

make prompt-guide initially stopped on receipts/local-flow-review.jsonl as material kernel dirt and recommended a force reset. That destructive duplicate gate was removed; native delivery care distinguishes source ownership from session telemetry. Prompt arrival also retires repeated Python retrieval bootstrap and stale broad proof instructions. The changed guide passes in the intentionally dirty worktree. No host implementation was added; these host/config edits are deletions only.

The pinned fkwu source and gitlink remain 0563230ff11ef60bef75cbd3444e69d40e75e679. No kernel or sibling suite ran. Application entry-image assembly and the changed route/index observations are the proof scope. Existing history, silence IDs, repair notes, original volume and private recovery copies remain intact.

Neighboring API-source observations remain attributed, not declared repaired by the Pulse movement: the old ideas handler measured serving times 3089.523, 533.955 and 1759.560 ms in one sequential internal/public/warm trace. Its underlying graph read took 26.877 ms and loaded 4560 rows; the compatibility owner still copies and scores the full portfolio before pagination. That source is further native API projection/host work, not a new accepted latency allowance. Public rollout readings follow the merged revision.
